articles.title: [UPDATE] Halloween: The Game Patches Out Sex Minigame — Dev Confirms 'Major Oversight'
articles.summary: Halloween: The Game developer IllFonic has patched out a sex mini-game after a gameplay clip went viral. Now, the studio has issued a statement.
body: "Players may have noticed that our latest hotfix removed the Two-Person Power-Up minigame. This was due to an unintended issue that allowed end game reinforcement characters to engage with the minigame, which was a major oversight on our part. We have more content and minigames coming in the near future but current focus is our attention on immediate game needs. Keep an eye on our socials for updates as they become available.”
ORIGINAL STORY: Halloween: The Game developer IllFonic appears to have patched out a sex minigame after a gameplay clip went viral.

The video game adaptation of the iconic 1970s slasher movie lets players have sex in a closet, but one video of this minigame featuring Samuel Loomis raised eyebrows given the character, who is in his fifties during the events of the game and is based on deceased actor Donald Pleasence’s likeness, can have sex with teenagers.

Halloween: The Game doesn’t actually launch fully until September 8, but those who bought the Halloween Deluxe Edition were able to play from this weekend, and it didn’t take long for players to notice the sex minigame.

articles.title: Fans Suspect DC's Official Wonder Woman Replacement Has Been Revealed
articles.summary: When James Gunn cast Adria Arjona ( Andor, Morbius ) for next year's Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow, reports pegged the actor as playing a relatively obscure DC character named Maxima.
body: The fact that Arjona is careful not to reveal which DC character she's playing in that video has only intensified speculation that we may already know who our next Wonder Woman is.

In a recently published video from Women's Health, Arjona walks viewers through her boxing and weightlifting routine, which sounds rigorous enough to tire an Amazonian superhero. "I'm enjoying the transformation, but it's hard work," Arjona says in the video. "I've never felt stronger, but it's hard. The excitement of playing the woman I'm playing gives me everything I need to wake up. Physically, it's exhausting, but it's all for the greater good."

Some fans have interpreted Arjona's comments as evidence that she will be the DCU's new Wonder Woman, based on her excitement levels and keeping her role secret. Fans argue she wouldn't be so excited to play Maxima, a relatively obscure character who prompted numerous 'Who Is Maxima in DC Comics?' articles across the internet.

articles.title: Christopher Nolan's Greatest Sci-Fi Action Masterpiece Is Officially Free to Watch on YouTube
articles.summary: With the immense critical praise surrounding The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan has firmly secured his place as a modern cinematic icon. His movies often feel like intricate puzzle boxes that demand to be solved, from the interlocking timelines of Dunkirk to the structural sleight-of-hand in The…
body: While there are plenty of examples, the film that forged Nolan’s identity as an auteur is inarguably Inception. Released in 2010, the film took the cerebral energy he cultivated in movies like Memento and Batman Begins and channeled it into a cinematic event unlike any other. Inception is a unique mesh of film noir, mystery, high-stakes thriller, and hard sci-fi. Nolan invited audiences into a dream world that you can experience for free on YouTube right now.

Inception remains remarkable in how Nolan makes such an absurd and complicated premise work. The dream mechanics of the narrative feed into some of the most inventive action sequences of Nolan's career, with a standout being the twisty hotel hallway sequence. Gordon-Levitt's Arthur fights his way through a corridor filled with thugs that has been built to rotate around the actors, imbuing the scene with the gravity-defying logic of a lucid dream all while carrying the visceral weight of a practical stunt.

articles.title: Zach Cregger Says He Feels Like He's 'Running for Office' Trying to Get Skeptical Resident Evil Fans 'Not to Call Me a LARPer'
articles.summary: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating skepticism from some fans about his movie adaptation of Capcom’s horror franchise.
body: Cregger, director of hugely popular horror movies Barbarian and Weapons, has faced scrutiny from Resident Evil fans ever since it was confirmed that his adaptation wouldn’t feature any characters from the video games, or tell any of the stories already told in the video games. Instead, Cregger has charted his own path, telling a horror story set in the world of Resident Evil that references some of the video games' tropes.
In an interview with The Playlist, Cregger outlined how it has felt to promote Resident Evil amid this backlash.
“I feel like I’ve been on somewhat of an apology tour,” he said. “I feel like I’m running for office, trying to get these people not to call me a LARPer.”

With Resident Evil now just a week away, Cregger is philosophical about fan attitude to the film. “Now, I’m just like, ‘You know what? See the movie.’” he told The Playlist. “If you still feel the same way after you’ve seen it, then whatever you think is fair. You’re going to decide if I’m an actual Resident Evil fan or a fake. What can I say? I think the movie is going to speak for itself.”
points: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating skepticism from some fans about his movie adaptation of Capcom’s horror franchise.

articles.title: New 85% on Metacritic Fantasy Action Game Just Shot Up to No. 1 on Steam Overnight
articles.summary: Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Capcom's latest action game set in a reimagined Edo-period Kyoto, debuted at No. 6 on Steam on Friday. SteamDB recorded 40,000 active players on the game's first day, an impressive feat when competing against fellow new release The Blood of Dawnwalker.
body: Twenty-four hours after its release, Onimusha: Way of the Sword surged to the No. 1 selling game on Steam, beating out both Halloween: The Game and WARDOGS. On Saturday, SteamDB recorded 74,575 active players. Way of the Sword marks Capcom's long-awaited return to the Onimusha story. The last mainline installment, Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams, came out in 2006.

While its No. 1 spot on Steam already suggests players are enjoying it, critics, too, have offered mostly positive reviews. At the time of writing, Way of the Sword has a Metacritic score of 85 and mostly positive reviews. Criticism mostly stems from the game's repetitive combat system.

Polygon's Giovanni Colantoni described the game as "a battle worth surviving," but only sometimes, citing routine fights, recycled bosses, and a progression system that doesn't feel rewarding enough. "It feels like a great 12-hour game stretched to an exhausting 25-hour one. Piecemeal progression and recycled bosses go hand-in-hand with repetitive rift-closing missions and backtracks through previous levels to clear busy work sidequests," Colantoni writes.
points: Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Capcom's latest action game set in a reimagined Edo-period Kyoto, debuted at No. 6 on Steam on Friday.

articles.title: 5 Most Exciting Thriller Movies of All Time
articles.summary: Great thrillers also explore lasting consequences, making it clear that none of the characters are safe while danger looms over them. With these elements in place, the art of a smart twist and the wonders of movie magic help tie everything together.
body: The most important ingredient for making an exciting thriller work is suspense. No amount of great pacing or compelling characters can make up for a lack of tension in a movie. Renowned thrillers like The Fugitive (1993) or Oldboy (2003) would fall flat without a visceral sense of urgency, which can translate into anxiety, excitement, or both.
With that in mind, here are the five most exciting thriller movies of all time, ranked.

Demme builds tension through close-quarter conversations. Although Bill feels menacing whenever he is onscreen, the suspense stems from Lecter’s refined cat-and-mouse game that Clarice must play to catch the killer. These interactions are fascinating, with Lecter constantly challenging Clarice to think like the suspect, while unraveling what makes her tick in exchange. As the hunt for Buffalo Bill continues, the use of multiple perspectives, red herrings, and spine-chilling sequences allows The Silence of the Lambs to crawl under our skin. It is a thriller that plays around with light and darkness to induce suffocation, while knowing when to go all out and indulge in gore-fueled carnage.

articles.title: The Batman Part 2 Goes in 'Another Totally Different Direction,' Robert Pattinson Teases
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson has suggested The Batman Part 2 will be a very different take on the DC superhero than we’ve seen before.
body: Pattinson is set to reprise his role as the Caped Crusader in The Batman Part 2, which has a February 18, 2028 release date. Assuming it hits that date, Part 2 will arrive in theaters just shy of six years after The Batman came out.

The movie is largely shrouded in mystery, but Pattinson has started to tease what to expect from it now he’s out and about promoting his new movie, Primetime. And in an interview captured by MYmovies on TikTok, Pattinson teased something quite different than what’s gone before.

“Matt just wrote this amazing script,” Pattinson said of The Batman co-writer and director Matt Reeves. “I think the first one was… it’s difficult to reinvent Batman as this new thing. And then to go in another totally different direction. I’m just looking at the playback on certain things… it looks different to the first one.

“It’s just amazing. It’s a quite radical change of the script. It’s cool that Warner’s behind it, and DC. It’s just crazy. It’s a really radical retelling of Batman. I think people are going to be excited by it.”

articles.title: Exodus Ending and Character Fates Change Based on Your Choices
articles.summary: Any time you look at or talk about Exodus, the upcoming space opera RPG from Archetype Entertainment, the Mass Effect comparisons start flying at light speed. I mean, Exodus narrative director Drew Karpyshyn played a major role as a writer and lead at BioWare to shape the stories of its biggest…
body: The parallels don't end with the Paladin/Immortal morality system or the romance and relationship dynamics that are going to drive the story, either. He hinted at how the decisions you make can impact Exodus' ending. Of course, that's not exclusive to BioWare games by any stretch, but when the Mass Effect 2's suicide mission is regarded as a series pinnacle, no one would blame to draw a quick comparison.

When I asked about the relationship systems in Exodus, Karpyshyn emphasized wanting to make them feel real and said it's about, "[M]aking their relationship with you grow, allowing it to evolve from the choices you've made, and realizing that the choices you make are going to bring some companions closer to you, but maybe push some companions farther away."

He took it one step further, and told me, "Without spoiling too much, we definitely want to have it impact how their storylines go." Then he took it another step further and concluded, "Depending on choices you make, by the end of the game, you might not have every companion with you that you started with. That's about all I can say!"
points: Any time you look at or talk about Exodus, the upcoming space opera RPG from Archetype Entertainment, the Mass Effect comparisons start flying at light speed.

articles.title: The Tetris Company confirms it had nothing to do with the White House's racist rip-off: 'we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them'
articles.summary: One of the many things making this feel like a particularly dumb epoch to be living through is the way the US government has taken to using videogames as a tool for self-aggrandizement and disseminating its pro-war and anti-immigration messages.
body: As a reminder, we've seen the Department of Homeland Security make a Pokémon mashup about how they "gotta catch 'em all", the White House use AI to dress Trump up as Master Chief from Halo after which Homeland Security decided "Destroy the Flood" was an appropriate recruitment message, and then the US government started using Call of Duty and Grand Theft Auto memes to promote its war in Iran.

Most recently, the White House launched an arcade section on its website containing terrible knock-offs of games like Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris. The Tetris game is particularly baffling. Reskinned as Build the Wall, it becomes a game of defeating a "zombie border siege" on the helpfully labeled "Southern Border" in case you missed the subtlety of its theming, where you stack up tetrominoes that never clear while zombies march toward the blocks.

The Tetris Company was motivated to respond. Posting on Instagram, it wrote, "At Tetris we believe in the power of connection and bringing people together, not dividing them. To our fans everywhere: we love you, we see you, and we're grateful to have you in our community."

articles.title: A hobby dev built a free, 3D galaxy map for Warhammer 40K that loads like lightning in your browser
articles.summary: Sometimes it's nice to just find something cool and fun and free on the internet, and the Cartographia Imperialis is just that: A 3D galaxy map of the Warhammer 40K Milky Way you can peruse in your browser.
body: It has the same simple, awe-inspiring majesty as Mass Effect's take on the concept, and you can explore it like an isometric videogame: Left click and drag to pan around, right click to rotate the camera, mouse wheel to zoom in and out. You can click on notable planets or regions to get little lore entries, or pull 'em up by name in the index to snap straight there on the map.

I'm not sure where creator Sami Gashi sourced the text for entries, pulling straight from official sources or paraphrasing in their own words, but I quite like the very in-universe prose. Take the entry for largely-unremarkable hive world Jouran, for example: "Its dossier is a reminder that strategic maps hide ordinary misery behind a clean point of light," the entry reads. "Jouran's value lies in quotas met, bodies counted, and local authorities willing to preserve output by any sanctioned means." That's good stuff.

Perhaps best of all, Cartographia Imperialis is completely free with no ads, and the map is shockingly lightweight for its graphical presentation and the current state of the internet. It loads super quick, and I haven't experienced any slowdown clicking around.

articles.title: Saber Interactive CCO says studio won't change its comms strategy after AI writer controversy
articles.summary: Saber Interactive CCO Tim Willits has confirmed the company has not revised its communications strategy despite its CEO telling the press that he "would have been happy to replace [a writer] with AI" after she claimed she was replaced by ChatGPT.
body: CEO Matthew Karch has since apologised to Stella Sacco, the writer at the centre of the Rideshare Stimulator AI controversy, but not before widespread public condemnation. He also shared a statement saying he'd had an "insightful week" but "the digital ecosystem thrives on outrage and surface-level takes".
"Sometimes we 'say what we mean' too much," Willits told PC Gamer, reflecting on the blunt comms from the studio's leadership.
When PC Gamer pressed directly on whether the recent backlash had prompted reflection, he reportedly said "no".

"I've been in the industry for so long, and there's always some dust up. People got mad at Saber because we put World War Z on Epic, and people were like, 'oh, Saber's destroying the industry'," Willits added.

articles.title: 18 years after Metal Gear Solid 4 first launched, a modder has shown off its first custom map, MGS3's Groznyj Grad
articles.summary: It already felt weird and wonderful to say that PC Gamer has reviewed Metal Gear Solid 4, a game for the personal computer. Now it gets even weirder: MGS4 mods are incoming, with TriggerHappy on YouTube already showing off a custom map in Kojima's 2008 stealth-action classic.
body: Back in 2021, modder Jayveer showed off a map ported from Metal Gear Arcade into Metal Gear Online 2, the multiplayer accompaniment to MGS4, but to my knowledge, TriggerHappy's is the first demonstration of a custom singleplayer map in MGS4.

It's 55 beautiful seconds of Old Snake crouch walking around Groznyj Grad, the iconic fortress level of Metal Gear Solid 3. Only now it's infested with Gecko walkers mooing their incongruous moos and showing off their distractingly shapely legs. Stupid, sexy Geckos. TriggerHappy laconically describes the gameplay as "initial testing for adding AI to a custom map."

The enemy AI certainly seems to work: Those Geckos are not happy to see Snake, and it's not because they believe a man of his age shouldn't be putting so much stress on his back and knees. It's unclear how TriggerHappy got this custom map working, or how far away we are from widely available map making tools, but this is an exciting first step in the realm of custom content for MGS4.
points: It already felt weird and wonderful to say that PC Gamer has reviewed Metal Gear Solid 4, a game for the personal computer.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker sold 1 million copies in just 3 days
articles.summary: On September 5, Rebel Wolves took to Twitter on the official Blood of Dawnwalker account to announce that the dark vampire RPG had already surpassed one million copies sold just three days after its September 2 launch.
body: I was in a Star Wars Zero Company-shaped hole during Dawnwalker's contemporaneous review period, but everyone on our team who played has been pretty pleased with this very Witcher-like RPG from ex-Witcher devs. Australian editor Shaun Prescott awarded it an 83% in his review, praising the storytelling and combat, but wishing that Rebel Wolves had gone harder on Dawnwalker's unique time mechanics.

"Blood of Dawnwalker is an effective piece of worldbuilding and storytelling then, but it doesn't make good on its promise as an innovative piece of RPG design," Shaun wrote. "Maybe Rebel Wolves worried that too many players would fall afoul of the passage of time and thus loosened its severity."

He was even more on the money than he could have realized when he wrote that: Some of the first mods for Dawnwalker do away with the time limit entirely. I appreciate the "have it your way" ethos mods can have, but I think a bit of friction can be a very good thing. I unilaterally declare PC Gamer to be a pro-time limits publication.

articles.title: Dutch artist responds to the White House's Build the Wall game with Build that Bridge
articles.summary: A Dutch artist has released Build that Bridge, a free browser game built as a direct response to Build the Wall, the Tetris-style minigame the White House launched on Arcade.Gov last week.
body: The Trump administration's site includes games inspired by old favourites. For example, Rio Run is a Snake-like game that wants you to collect a chain of prisoners in orange jumpsuits, tallying a "deported" count at the end of each run, and Build the Wall: Zombie Border Siege, a Tetris riff where players stack bricks against incoming "aliens" at the "Southern Border".

Whereas the White House version has players stack blocks into a wall, artist and social designer Wouter Sieuwerts's version, Build that Bridge, uses the same mechanics in reverse: clearing lines grows a bridge from both riverbanks toward the middle.
"Just as the colonisation of America was turned into child's play, the White House now makes a game out of excluding migrants," Sieuwerts said.

"But play is precisely how you discover the world and get to know new people and customs. So for everyone who would rather build bridges than walls, I made Build that Bridge. Play along and make yourself heard."

articles.title: Double Fine's first game since leaving Xbox is a comedy bus-driving sim called Thank You Bus Driver
articles.summary: Double Fine's first game since leaving Xbox, Thank You Bus Driver, is a comedy sim about a reckless bus driver just trying to be appreciated.
body: Double Fine's first game in its new post-Xbox era is Thank You Bus Driver.

Described as a comedy simulation game, the game - listed only as "coming soon" on Steam - sees you take on the role of a "reckless" bus driver in which you're encouraged to "drive fast, slap faster, and toss any rulebreakers out of your bus to reach true victory: being appreciated".
"Take on the role of a town’s rules-driven (and reckless) bus driver in Thank You Bus Driver!" the Steam description teases.

"Getting to your next stop is all that matters. That might mean pulling up your map mid-turn or it might mean a shortcut through the corn field. Avoiding pedestrians, incoming traffic, or the fence directly in front of you is optional."

Make way for the legendary delinquent - Kanji Tatsumi in Persona 4 Revival, launching on February 18, 2027, for PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X|S, Xbox Game Pass, and PC (Steam).
